title: Inference Failure Signal Correlator and Latency-weighted Trace Sampling Policy
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Problem: Multiple upstream workstreams are instrumenting errors (HTTP/gRPC codes, model rejections, KV cache misses, queue wait times) independently, but on-call and SRE teams lack a consolidated, correlated view that surfaces multi-signal failure modes. This ticket implements a cross-surface signal correlator and an adaptive, latency-weighted trace sampling policy so high-value traces (errors with heavy customer impact or tail latency) are retained without overwhelming storage or KBs. Goals: 1) Compute a runtime correlation matrix that links error classes (timeouts, overload, model errors, HTTP/gRPC statuses) to latency percentiles and resource signals. 2) Implement a sampling policy that increases trace retention for correlated high-latency/error slices and for rare but severe model-rejection patterns. 3) Expose a new dashboard and tagging conventions for analysts to pivot by signal combinations. Success criteria: consolidated dashboard available in console, sampling policy deployed to staging with <10% added ingest, SRE & oncall signoff, and documented playbook for triage flows.
acceptance_criteria: Correlation matrix computation running in observability pipeline and updating every 5 minutes
Trace sampler implemented as a hook in request ingress and respects route-level overrides
Sampling preserves traces for: top 5% latency requests, any request with HTTP 5xx / gRPC UNKNOWN/INTERNAL, model rejection/error responses, and requests with queue wait time > 200ms
Dashboard shows pairwise signal correlations, conditional latency CDFs, and a ranked list of emergent slices
End-to-end test demonstrating <10% increase in trace ingress at staging under synthetic load
Runbook updated with new triage steps and examples linking correlated slices to remediation actions

technical_notes: Correlation approach: compute pairwise conditional probability P(error_type | latency_bucket) and mutual information across signals using a rolling 5-minute window

Sampling policy: baseline reservoir sampling for 1% global traces, augmented by multipliers: x10 for traces matching 'severe' slices, x5 for top 1% latency per-route, route-level caps to limit per-route ingestion
Latency-weighting: use exponential weighting where samples from higher latency percentiles have higher retention probability; weight = min(20, exp((p95_latency - baseline)/sigma))
Backpressure safety: enforce global hard cap on sampler throughput and fallback to deterministic sampling when collector queue > 75%
Span tagging: add fields 'signal.correlator.slice' and 'signal.correlator.score' to the root span so downstream processors can group traces without re-computing
Data retention: retain high-score traces for 90 days, normal traces for 7 days; retention configurable via release flags
Privacy: ensure no PII is added by correlator; existing PII scrubbing pipeline runs post-sampling.
testing_plan: Unit tests for correlation matrix aggregator with synthetic time-series inputs
Integration test: end-to-end from ingress hook -> collector -> pipeline -> dashboard under 50 rps synthetic workload
Load test in staging with 5x production-ish traffic to validate sampler caps and confirm <10% extra trace ingress
Chaos test: simulate bursty model rejection rate and validate sampler increases retention for correlated slices
SRE runbook walkthrough with a live incident replay using recorded traces
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): deploy sampling hook to 5% of production routes with conservative multipliers and monitor ingest rates for 48 hours
Phase 2 (staged): expand to 30% of routes, enable correlation matrix export to dashboard, collect SRE feedback
Phase 3 (global): enable for all routes with adaptive multipliers, switch dashboard to primary view, notify customers via changelog
Rollback: disable sampling multipliers and revert to baseline reservoir sampling; dashboard will show reduced high-score traces but system will be stable
